messages:
jessica_c: @here Kestrel Health flagged an urgent blocker in the SI integration. Their security/compliance team requires that model keys be stored in a customer HSM and that inference traffic for private deployment go through a locked-down on-prem egress gateway. Customer target go‑live in ~2 weeks. Can eng + partners triage network + key management impacts?

mike_s: +1, can we get the exact ask from the SI (ports, cert checks, HSM interface)? If keys must never leave customer KMS/HSM, we need to confirm support for external KMS wraps and how dedicated/private runtime will access the keys.

jessica_c: SI sent a quick note: they want AWS CloudHSM/Thales HSM via PKCS#11, and a private VPC‑peered path is not allowed — they must route through an on‑prem egress gateway appliance that performs TLS interception for DLP. They also mentioned a compliance restriction: model weights cannot be persisted on vendor-managed SSDs unless encrypted with customer key.

elaine_p: tagging the SI PM @mike_s — partner expects us to provide a deployment pattern doc they can include in their runbook. Timeline: partner needs final arch by EOD Friday for their internal signoffs. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sanjay_m: A few immediate red flags: 1) PKCS#11 support — our runtime currently supports KMS integrations via REST (CloudKMS, AzureKeyVault). PKCS#11 is not in upstream path. 2) On‑prem egress gateway + TLS interception could break mTLS between runtime and model shards (if we route RPC over that path). 3) Persistent storage encryption with customer keys — we can support envelope encryption but need key wrapping support from customer KMS with a secure bridge.

mike_s: Ok — propose quick triage + decision log:
- Confirm exact HSM vendor/APIs (CloudHSM vs Thales vs Vault HSM).
- Verify whether customer will accept an HSM proxy (a small shim VM in their environment that exposes a REST KMS facade backed by PKCS#11).
- Confirm what traffic flows must traverse on‑prem gateway vs what can remain direct (metrics/telemetry vs model weights replication).

jessica_c: SI PM says they can run an HSM proxy VM in their DMZ. They prefer no persistent S3-style uploads visible to vendor account. They want proof that runtime will not exfiltrate unencrypted model shards.

elaine_p: I'll coordinate with partner PM to get HSM vendor details and their network diagram. Also looping legal on evidence artifacts for non-exfiltration.

sanjay_m: For immediate engineering actions: If partner can host an HSM proxy that speaks our REST KMS API, we can implement key wrap/unwarp flow in 48–72h (short patch). Otherwise full PKCS#11 integration is a 3–4 week effort. For the network side, we need to know which ports the gateway allows outbound and whether it performs packet rewriting.

mike_s: I'm drafting an architecture note that covers two patterns: A) HSM-proxy + direct peering (preferred) and B) PKCS#11 native (fallback). Includes a checklist for SI: firewall ports (443, 22 for ops?), allowed SNI values, and signed cert pinning requirements.

deploy-bot: Ticket #INC-8421 created: "Kestrel SI — HSM proxy + on‑prem gateway triage" assigned to eng-platform. Link: https://tickets.example.com/INC-8421

jessica_c: Thanks — immediate ask for eng: can we commit to producing the arch note + checklist by EOD Friday? Partner will freeze their runbook then.

sanjay_m: We can do a short arch note + checklist by Friday if partner confirms HSM vendor today. I'll allocate time for the key-wrap PoC (48h) once vendor is confirmed.

elaine_p: Partner confirmed Thales Luna and an on‑prem BlueGate appliance. I'll DM the configs and network diagram now.

mike_s: Great. Action items:
- elaine_p: collect vendor docs + network diagram (today)
- sanjay_m: quick feasibility for HSM-proxy + key-wrap PoC (48–72h)
- mike_s: architecture note + runbook checklist (EOD Friday)
- jessica_c: update customer on blocker status and expected mitigation timeline

jessica_c: I'll tell the customer we have a plan and expect arch+checklist by Friday. Thanks all — ping me if anything blocks. :raised_hands:
